:::{#thm-rank-product}
#### Multiplying on the right cannot increase the rank

If $\matr{A}$ is $m \times n$ and $\matr{B}$ is $n \times k$, then

$$
\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A} \matr{B}) \le \operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}).
$$

:::

::: proof

**$\mathcal{C}(\matr{A} \matr{B}) \subseteq \mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$.**
Any vector in $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A} \matr{B})$ is $(\matr{A} \matr{B})\,\vecf{x}$
for some $\vecf{x} \in \reals^k$ (@def-column-space), and

$$
\ba
(\matr{A} \matr{B})\,\vecf{x}
&= \matr{A}\,(\matr{B} \vecf{x})
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\ea
$$

is $\matr{A}$ times the vector $\matr{B} \vecf{x} \in \reals^n$,
so it is in $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$.

**Compare dimensions.**
Both column spaces are subspaces (@thm-column-space-span), so

$$
\ba
\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A} \matr{B})
&= \dim\paren{\mathcal{C}(\matr{A} \matr{B})}
&& \text{(@thm-rank-dim)}
\\
&\le \dim\paren{\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})}
&& \text{(@thm-dim-bound, part 2)}
\\
&= \operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}).
&& \text{(@thm-rank-dim)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-rank-product}
#### A product can lose rank

Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{A} \matr{B}
= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 0 + 0 \cd 1 & 1 \cd 0 + 0 \cd 0 \\ 0 \cd 0 + 0 \cd 1 & 0 \cd 0 + 0 \cd 0 \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

$\matr{A}$ has rank $1$, but $\matr{A} \matr{B}$ has rank $0$,
so the inequality in @thm-rank-product can be strict.
With the $2 \times 2$ identity in place of $\matr{B}$,
$\matr{A} \matr{I} = \matr{A}$ keeps rank $1$, and the inequality is an equality.

:::
